class.name: JarVoxelVolume
class.brief_description: A smooth voxel volume: terrain, a planet, a moon or a prop, defined by a signed distance field.
class.description: JarVoxelVolume samples [member sdf] into an octree and meshes it into chunks with level of detail. Everything happens in the volume's local space, so a volume can be moved, rotated and animated freely (for example a moon orbiting a planet), and any number of volumes can exist in one scene. All volumes share one worker thread pool. Level of detail follows every [JarVoxelViewer] in the scene (or the active camera if there is none). Edit the volume with [method sphere_edit] or [method modify]; edits are queued and applied on a background thread. To find the volume behind a physics hit, use [method JarVoxelChunk.get_volume] on the collider's chunk.

method.name: edit
method.description: Combines [param sdf], placed with the global [param transform] (position, rotation and uniform scale), with the volume using [param operation]. The affected region is derived from [method JarSignedDistanceField.get_bounds], so the SDF must be bounded. [param material] (0-3) is painted onto changed voxels, [code]-1[/code] keeps existing materials. [param smoothness] is the blend radius of the smooth operations; [code]0[/code] uses the voxel size. Edits are queued and applied on a background thread. [codeblock] var box := JarBoxSdf.new() box.extent = Vector3(2, 4, 2) volume.edit(box, JarVoxelVolume.SDF_OPERATION_UNION, Transform3D(Basis(Vector3.UP, PI / 4), hit_position)) [/codeblock]

method.name: get_height_at
method.description: Returns the height of [param global_position] above [member sea_level], measured along the volume's up direction (see [member up_mode]).

method.name: get_up_direction_at
method.description: Returns the global-space up direction at [param global_position] (see [member up_mode]). Useful to orient a character on a planet.

method.name: is_building
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] while the background worker is rebuilding the octree or applying edits. Edits requested meanwhile are queued and applied afterwards.

method.name: is_meshing
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] while chunk meshes are queued, being generated, or waiting to be applied. When both this and [method is_building] return [code]false[/code], the terrain around the player is up to date.

method.name: modify
method.description: Modifies the terrain using another [JarSignedDistanceField] instance at a given [code]position[/code], with the specified [code]operation[/code]. The [code]radius[/code] determines the affected area. If [code]sdf[/code] is [code]null[/code], a sphere of [code]radius[/code] is used. [code]material[/code] (0-3) is painted onto the affected voxels as a one-hot weight in the vertex color, which the chunk shader blends as materials; pass [code]-1[/code] to keep the existing material weights.

method.name: spawn_debug_spheres_in_bounds
method.description: Spawns debug spheres within the specified [code]range[/code] around [code]position[/code] to visualize terrain bounds or other metrics.

method.name: sphere_edit
method.description: Adds or subtracts a spherical volume from the terrain. The center is defined by [code]position[/code], and [code]radius[/code] defines its size. Set [code]union[/code] to [code]true[/code] to add, or [code]false[/code] to subtract. [code]material[/code] (0-3) selects the material painted onto the edited voxels (see [method modify]); pass [code]-1[/code] to keep the existing material.

members.member: Scene used for singular chunk. Will be duplicated once for each rendered chunk.
Enables/disables automatic LOD updates when a [JarVoxelViewer] moves.
Distance in world units used to determine whether LODs need to be updated based on player movement.
Determines number of different LOD levels. Higher number means smoother transition between close and far LODs.
Number of LOD rings (shells) around the player. Affects how much terrain is loaded based on proximity.
Number of vertices in the smallest subdivision of the chunk.
Scaling factor for the octree used in terrain chunk management and LOD computation.

Main-thread time per frame, in milliseconds, spent uploading chunk colliders to the physics engine. Colliders nearest the player are uploaded first. Higher values make collision available sooner after the terrain changes, at the cost of frame time.

When greater than [code]0.0[/code], physics colliders are only generated for chunks within this distance of the camera, on top of the usual LOD-based collider rules. Since collider generation is one of the most expensive parts of chunk updates, this can be a large performance win. Set it comfortably larger than the range at which physics interactions are needed. [code]0.0[/code] disables the distance cull (original behaviour).
Optional hard cap on how many chunk colliders are uploaded per second. [code]0[/code] means no cap: uploads are limited only by [member performance_collider_budget_ms].
Defines additional objects or modifications applied to the terrain, such as grass, rocks, or decorations.
The signed distance field ([JarSignedDistanceField]) used to define terrain shape.
Height 0 for [method get_height_at] and population height ranges: the planet radius for [constant UP_MODE_RADIAL], or the offset along [member up_axis] for [constant UP_MODE_AXIS].
Size of the terrain grid in chunks. Increasing this value expands the rendered area.
Local up direction when [member up_mode] is [constant UP_MODE_AXIS]; also the fallback at the exact center of a radial volume.
Local-space center: the planet center for [constant UP_MODE_RADIAL], and the origin of height measurement for [constant UP_MODE_AXIS].

How "up" is defined inside the volume, used for population rules (slope and height ranges) and [method get_up_direction_at]. [constant UP_MODE_AXIS] for flat worlds, [constant UP_MODE_RADIAL] for planets.

constants.constant: Up is the constant [member up_axis] (flat worlds).
Up points away from [member up_center] (planets and moons).
Carves the shape out of the volume.
Keeps only the part of the volume inside the shape.
Adds the shape with a smooth fillet of radius [code]smoothness[/code].
Carves the shape with smoothly rounded edges.
